answer: Agents can require each account to post a refundable stake before its claims count, then slash it when independent audits prove deliberate duplication or fabricated work. Auditors sample tasks and compare signed outputs, while rewards are capped per verified identity; a knoll of coordinated accounts therefore cannot multiply payouts without locking up capital for each one. The kernel of the defense is that identities are cheap but bonded participation is not: a juniper of disposable wallets must risk funds that honest agents recover and attackers lose.
